results.question: Can we switch from NB54360 to the cheaper NB54361-L?
results.answer:
No — NB54361-L is not approved and must not be used. It was proposed as a cost-down substitute for NB54360 on PSM-28 Rev 2 but was **rejected** (DEC-117, decided by Vishwas, 2025-03-12). It failed the thermal soak test: it hit thermal shutdown at 68°C under full load, below the 70°C ambient requirement for sealed avionics enclosures (TR-112). The alternate's approval status is REJECTED.

The ₹60/unit saving (₹190 vs ₹250, per quote Q-102) is not worth it — the part cannot meet the thermal derating requirement. NB54360 remains the approved regulator.

results.question: Who decided against using NB54361-L, and when?
results.answer: Vishwas decided against NB54361-L on 2025-03-12, recorded as DEC-117 (rejected as a substitute for NB54360 on PSM-28 Rev 2, because it failed thermal soak — hit thermal shutdown at 68C under full load, per TR-112).

results.question: Which test showed NB54361-L failing, and at what ambient temperature?
results.answer: NB54361-L failed in the thermal derating test TR-112 (run under qualification procedure TP-PSM-07) on PSM-28 Rev 2. It hit thermal shutdown at 68C ambient under full load in the sealed enclosure, failing the 70C ambient requirement. (Confirmed by DEC-117, which rejected it as a substitute for NB54360.)

results.question: Is MX-3360 approved as a replacement for NB54360?
results.answer: No. MX-3360 is not approved as a replacement for NB54360. The only recorded decision about it is DX-95a76cf6, outcome **proposed** — it was merely identified as the most likely second source (from Sahyadri/Meridian Analog) on 2026-10-12. There is no approved decision. Per the alternates listing, MX-3360's basis is "distributor_crossref" — "Suggested by distributor as functional equivalent; not an engineering approval." No test, quote, or chat message constitutes approval, and none is recorded as such. So MX-3360 is not an approved substitute for NB54360.

results.question: What caused the brownouts at Nilgiri and how were they fixed?
results.answer:
Cause: The PDU-28 Rev B units at Nilgiri were running firmware 2.2, whose power-good timing was too tight. As Sai diagnosed in SUP-1042, "firmware 2.2 waits 4 ms for power-good; the regulator soft-start needs up to 4 ms plus margin" — so on a cold morning start the unit tripped a brownout before the regulator had settled. Two units restarted this way.

Fix: The bug was corrected in the pmic_seq.c firmware module (FW-PMIC-SEQ), shipped as firmware 2.3.1, which was deployed to all 220 Nilgiri Rev B units. Per the #fw-team Slack log, there were no further brownouts after 2.3.1, and the cold-start test was folded into the Firmware 2.4 release so it stays covered.

Key records: SUP-1042 (ticket), FW-PMIC-SEQ (pmic_seq.c), PRJ-FW24 (Firmware 2.4).

results.question: What is Konkan Naval unhappy about, and which order is at stake?
results.answer:
Konkan Naval Electronics is unhappy that 6 of their BCU-24 Rev A battery chargers stop reporting CAN telemetry after a cold start, and only recover after a power cycle — so their power management system loses battery state each time. The root cause (SUP-1057) is the CT-1051 CAN transceiver entering bus-off during the cold-start inrush, with no firmware bus-off recovery. They will hold acceptance of the order unless a fix is confirmed before delivery.

Order at stake: SO-884 — 60 BCU-24 Rev A units, value ₹19,200,000, due 2026-11-25 (build BO-0415).

- Ticket: SUP-1057.json — customer reports the telemetry drop; root cause is the CT-1051 transceiver bus-off with no recovery; fix (watchdog bus-off recovery) can ship in Firmware 2.4 if prioritised.
- Order: SO-884, qty 60, unit price 32000.0, value 1920000.0, due 2026-11-25, revision BCU-24-A, build BO-0415.
